title: Foundations: Bossa Vocal - The Complete Guide
summary: What Bossa Vocal is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Bossa Vocal songs: Bossa nova vocals float: soft Portuguese (or English) melodies over nylon-string guitar and a swaying samba pulse. João Gilberto's whisper and Astrud Gilberto's cool made it a world sound.

History: Born on Rio's beaches in the late 1950s: Antônio Carlos Jobim's songs, João Gilberto's guitar beat, Vinicius de Moraes's poetry. Getz/Gilberto (1964) and The Girl from Ipanema made it a global craze.

How the songs work: Bossa Vocal favors the keys of F, G, C, D. Common forms include AABA with a floating, behind-the-beat vocal; Portuguese verse, English chorus in crossover versions. Players should master the gilberto beat: thumb bass, syncopated chords first, then singing just behind the beat. Nylon-string, often no capo.

title: The Girl from Ipanema - Bossa Vocal Song Study
summary: Harmonic blueprint and playing guide for The Girl from Ipanema by Antônio Carlos Jobim (1962).
body:
The Girl from Ipanema — Antônio Carlos Jobim, 1962. The second-most recorded pop song in history.

HARMONIC BLUEPRINT (study chart, key of C):
Cm9 | F13 | A#m6 | A#m6

This study chart uses the 'Bossa minor' progression, the Bossa Vocal workhorse, to map how songs like this move. Form: aaba with a floating, behind-the-beat vocal. Listen for nylon-string fingerpicking, nails short — it is the fingerprint of the style.

TO PLAY IT: set your tempo to the Bossa Vocal pocket, voice the chords cleanly, and let nylon-string fingerpicking, nails short. Nylon-string, often no capo. (Song facts: title/artist/year are documented public records; the chart is an original study arrangement.)
